title: Can you trust ancestry DNA kits?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: diagram that shows all the members of a family, usually over a long period of time, and how they are related to each other
the origins of your family; your ancestors who lived a long time ago

keywords.term: take (it) with a pinch of salt
keywords.def: do not believe that something is completely accurate or true; be doubtful or sceptical about something
relatives who lived in the past
social, cultural and linguistic characteristics shared by a large group of people

sentences.en: Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好。这里是BBC英语教学的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. Nowadays, it's popular to find out more about your family history by tracing your family tree – a diagram that shows all the members of a family over a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔。我是贝丝。如今，通过追溯家谱——一种展示一个家族在漫长时间里所有成员的图表——来了解更多家族历史非常流行。

sentences.en: What do you know about your family history, Beth?
sentences.zh: 贝丝，你对自己的家族历史了解多少？

sentences.en: Well, my Mum actually did our family tree, and she found a lot of our ancestors had emigrated to the United States.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实是我妈妈做的家谱，她发现我们的许多祖先曾移民到美国。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I don't know much more than that.
sentences.zh: 不过，是的，除了这些我了解得并不多。

sentences.en: What about you? Well, I'm lucky to have an unusual surname, so it's quite easy to trace my ancestors and somebody in my family has gone back to 1700 and found somebody with my name.
sentences.zh: 你呢？我挺幸运的，有一个不常见的姓氏，所以追溯祖先相当容易，家族里有人甚至查到了1700年，找到了一个和我同名的人。

sentences.en: Wow, that's amazing. Well, the internet has made it easier to find the historical records needed to research your ancestry - the origins of your family.
sentences.zh: 哇，那太神奇了。互联网让人类更容易找到研究你的祖先——即家族起源——所需的历史记录。

sentences.en: But what if you want to find out about a time before historical records began?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你想了解历史记录诞生之前的时期呢？

sentences.en: Luckily, some companies now offer to trace your ancestry using DNA.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，现在一些公司提供利用DNA来追溯祖先的服务。

sentences.en: DNA is the cellular information that's passed down from parents to children telling the body how to create life.
sentences.zh: DNA是代代相传的细胞信息，它告诉身体如何创造生命。

sentences.en: Listener, Chris, from the UK, recently took a DNA ancestry test.
sentences.zh: 来自英国的听众克里斯最近做了一次DNA祖先测试。

sentences.en: When the test returned some unexpected results, Chris called BBC Radio 4 programme, Sliced Bread, wondering how accurate they really were: Not so long ago I sent off a home DNA testing kit and the results that came back were broadly in line with expectations, but it had some little glitches in there which made me think, is this accurate?
sentences.zh: 当测试得出一些意想不到的结果时，克里斯给BBC广播四台的节目《Sliced Bread》打去了电话，想知道这些测试到底有多准确：不久前我寄出了一套家用DNA测试套件，返回的结果大致符合预期，但里面有一些小故障，这让我不禁思考，这到底准不准呢？

sentences.en: Or is it to be taken with a pinch of salt?
sentences.zh: 还是说应该对其持怀疑态度？

sentences.en: Chris wondered whether his results were accurate, or whether to take them with a pinch of salt, an idiom meaning to doubt something is completely true.
sentences.zh: 克里斯想知道他的结果是否准确，还是应该对它们“持保留态度”（take with a pinch of salt），这是一个表示对某事是否完全真实感到怀疑的习语。

sentences.en: So, in this programme we'll discuss how accurate DNA ancestry tracing is, and, as usual, we'll learn some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这个节目中，我们将讨论DNA祖先追溯有多准确，并且像往常一样，我们会学到一些实用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember, you can find all the vocabulary for this programme on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本节目的所有词汇。

sentences.en: First though, I have a question for you, Beth.
sentences.zh: 不过首先，贝丝，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: One reason to be cautious about DNA ancestry tests is that humans are very similar to each other.
sentences.zh: 对DNA祖先测试需要保持谨慎的原因之一是，人类彼此非常相似。

sentences.en: Most of your DNA is identical with every other person on earth, and it's only the tiny amount of difference that accounts for all genetic variations between humans.
sentences.zh: 你绝大部分的DNA与地球上的其他每个人都是相同的，只有极少量的差异构成了人与人之间的所有基因变异。

sentences.en: So, exactly how much DNA do humans share with each other?
sentences.zh: 那么，人类彼此之间究竟共享了多少DNA？

sentences.en: I am going to guess 99.9%. OK. well we'll find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 我猜是99.9%。好的，我们在节目的后面会揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Another problem for research based on DNA is agreeing on the meaning of words like 'ancestry' and 'ethnicity'.
sentences.zh: 基于DNA研究的另一个问题是对“祖先”和“族群”这类词义的达成共识。

sentences.en: Here, genealogist, Louise Baldock explains the difference between these words to BBC Radio 4 programme, 'Sliced Bread': So 'ancestry' is really about people, it's about your actual forebears.
sentences.zh: 在这里，家谱学者路易丝·巴尔多克向BBC广播四台节目《Sliced Bread》解释了这些词的区别：所以“祖先”（ancestry）其实是关于人的，它是指你真正的祖先（forebears）。

sentences.en: Your ' ethnicity',you would probably think of in geographical terms, maybe which continent or which region your 'people' came from.
sentences.zh: 至于你的“族群”（ethnicity），你可能会从地理角度来思考，也许是你的“族人”来自哪个大洲或哪个地区。

sentences.en: Like 'ancestors', the term forebears means actual people - the relatives in your family from a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 就像“祖先”（ancestors）一样，forebears这个词指的是真正的人——你家族中很久以前的亲戚。

sentences.en: But Louise is more interested in the term, ethnicity – the shared culture, language and traditions of a group of people – and this is closely connected to a geographical location.
sentences.zh: 但路易丝对“族群”（ethnicity）这个词更感兴趣——它是一群人共享的文化、语言和传统——这与地理位置紧密相连。

sentences.en: And it's this question of geography which interested BBC presenter, Greg Foot.
sentences.zh: 正是这个地理问题引起了BBC主持人格雷格·福特的兴趣。

sentences.en: Greg sent DNA samples to two different companies.
sentences.zh: 格雷格将DNA样本寄给了两家不同的公司。

sentences.en: The results from the first company matched what he already knew about his family, that the past five generations came from England.
sentences.zh: 第一家公司的结果与他对自己家族已有的了解相吻合，即过去五代人来自英格兰。

sentences.en: But listen to what happens when Louise Baldock revealed the results of Greg's second DNA test on his BBC Radio 4 show, Sliced Bread: It's going to blow your mind! [OK].
sentences.zh: 但听听当路易丝·巴尔多克在BBC广播四台节目《Sliced Bread》上公布格雷格的第二个DNA测试结果时发生了什么：这会让你大开眼界！[好的]。

sentences.en: Can I tell you what you're looking at? Yes, please do.
sentences.zh: 我能告诉你你看到的是什么吗？好的，请讲。

sentences.en: It says that you are, first of all, 66% north and west Europe, but explicitly that doesn't refer to the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 上面说你首先有66%来自北欧和西欧，但明确指出这不包括英国。

sentences.en: OK, that's a wide geographical area. 27.5% Irish, Scottish and Welsh, but again, explicitly not English.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那是一个广阔的地理区域。27.5%属于爱尔兰、苏格兰和威士忌，不对，是苏格兰和威尔士，但同样明确指出不是英国。

sentences.en: The second company's DNA test blows Greg's mind – it makes him very excited and surprised.
sentences.zh: 第二家公司的DNA测试让格雷格大开眼界——这让他感到非常兴奋和惊讶。

sentences.en: There's no evidence of his ancestors being English at all!
sentences.zh: 根本没有证据表明他的祖先是英国人！

sentences.en: Actually, companies compare DNA with other samples in their database, and since companies use different databases, it's not too surprising that Greg's results were so different – unlike his actual DNA.
sentences.zh: 实际上，公司会将DNA与数据库中的其他样本进行比较，由于各家公司使用不同的数据库，格雷格的结果差异如此之大也就不足为奇了——这与他实际的DNA并不矛盾。

sentences.en: Speaking of which, what was the answer to your question, Neil?
sentences.zh: 说到这儿，你问题的答案是什么，尼尔？

sentences.en: I asked you what percentage of human DNA is shared by everyone, and what was your answer, Beth?
sentences.zh: 我问你人类DNA有多少百分比是所有人共享的，你的答案是什么，贝丝？

sentences.en: I said 99.9%. Well, you must be very clever, because the answer is correct.
sentences.zh: 我说的是99.9%。嗯，你一定很聪明，因为答案是正确的。

sentences.en: Well done! Right, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned starting with family tree, a diagram showing all the members of a family Ancestry refers to the origins of a family.
sentences.zh: 干得好！好，让我们回顾一下我们学过的词汇，首先是“家谱”（family tree），一张显示家族所有成员的图表。“祖先”（Ancestry）指的是家族的起源。

sentences.en: If you take something with a pinch of salt, you don't believe it's completely true.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某事“持保留态度”（take with a pinch of salt），就说明你并不认为它完全真实。

sentences.en: Forebears are relatives who lived in the past.
sentences.zh: “先辈”（Forebears）是指生活在过去的亲戚。

sentences.en: Ethnicity means the social, cultural and linguistic characteristics shared by a group of people.
sentences.zh: “族群”（Ethnicity）意味着一群人所共享的社会、文化和语言特征。

sentences.en: And finally, if something blows your mind, it makes you excited or surprised.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果某事“让你大开眼界”（blows your mind），它会让你感到兴奋或惊讶。

sentences.en: Once again our six minutes are up, but why not head over to the BBC Learning English website where you'll find a worksheet and quiz especially for this programme.
sentences.zh: 我们的6分钟时间又到了，为什么不去BBC英语教学网站看一看呢？在那里你会找到专门为这个节目准备的练习册和测验。

sentences.en: See you there soon! Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 很快在那里见到你！再见！
